title: Sharps and instruments in theatre
audience: Operating-theatre clinical staff. Theatre cleaning contractors read only the section headed What cleaners do and follow the theatre instructions for everything else.
learningOutcomes: Describe how a sharp instrument moves between a surgeon and an assistant without being handed directly.
State the disposal rules for used needles and disposable blades in the theatre.
State the steps a cleaner takes when they find a sharp in the theatre.

instruction.heading: Scope of the surgical points
instruction.body: This lesson covers how sharps are handled in the theatre. The surgical technique described in the theatre document is for trained theatre clinicians working in the operating setting. It is not a cleaning method and must not be applied to the work of cleaning contractors. Cleaners follow only the final section of this lesson.

instruction.heading: Moving sharps between clinicians
instruction.body: A sharp is never handed across by hand between a surgeon and an assistant. The surgeon places sharps safely. Each sharp travels in a dish reserved for sharps, and the dish holds one sharp at any moment. Where two surgeons work at once, each keeps a personal dish. The learner guide sets the baseline: a sharp is not handed to another person by hand, and is placed in a puncture-resistant tray for handover. Any dish the theatre uses must meet that puncture-resistant standard.

instruction.heading: Blades and needles
instruction.body: Where practicable, use one-piece disposable scalpels so that no blade has to be pulled from a reusable handle. Where a removable blade is used, detach it with an appropriate device rather than with the fingers. Lift a needle with grooved forceps or a needle holder, never with the fingers. Do not resheath or recap a used needle. Spent needles and single-use sharps go into a facility-approved bin without delay.

instruction.heading: Glove tears and needlestick events
instruction.body: When a glove splits or a needle pricks someone, take the glove off, scrub the hands with the surgical solution, fit a fresh glove, and take the implicated needle or tool out of the sterile zone. Address a needle prick or a mucous membrane splash once it is safe to do so. The learner guide adds the wound steps: clean the wound using soap and water, press on any bleeding, cover the wound with a waterproof dressing, tell the supervisor straight away, and complete the incident report. For wounds, the learner guide governs.

instruction.heading: Containers and filling
instruction.body: Sharps containers must be approved, puncture-resistant and water-proof, clearly labelled, and usable with one hand. The theatre document says to close a container when it is three-quarters full. That figure is not an Australian rule and is not adopted. Use the facility fill line. Do not reopen a sealed container, and do not place a sharps container where it blocks cleaning. Sharps waste leaves the site with a licensed operator, who destroys it by incineration.

instruction.heading: Surgical technique not used here
instruction.body: Several surgical points in the theatre document, including how to close the skin, how to manage drainage and how to use laser cutting, are not reproduced in these lessons. They belong to surgical training and are not support-worker content.

instruction.heading: What cleaners do
instruction.body: A cleaner never picks up a sharp by hand, and never recaps or bends a needle. If a sharp is found on the floor, in linen or in a dish, stop, keep others away, alert the nearest theatre team member, and let them retrieve it with an approved tool. Record the find as a hazard. A glove torn during cleaning is replaced at once, after hand washing.

procedure: Clinical staff: use a sharps dish for every transfer, with one sharp at a time.
Clinical staff: place a used needle into the sharps container without recapping it.
Clinical staff: if a glove splits, scrub the hands, fit a fresh glove, and take the affected tool out of the sterile zone.
Cleaner: stop, keep others clear of the sharp, and alert the nearest theatre team member.
Cleaner: wait for retrieval with an approved tool, then record the hazard.

workedExamples.situation: During a case, a scrub nurse hands a scalpel blade directly to the surgeon.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is wrong, and what should happen instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: Hand-to-hand passing is not the approved method. The blade belongs in the sharps dish, one sharp at a time, and the surgeon takes it from the dish.

workedExamples.situation: After a case, a cleaner sees a used needle on the floor beside the table.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not touch it with the hand or try to recap it. Alert the nearest theatre team member, who retrieves it with an approved tool. Record it as a hazard.

equipmentAndPpe: Sharps dish and puncture-resistant transfer tray
Approved sharps container with a facility fill line
Gloves in the size and type the theatre plan lists, and spare gloves
Grooved forceps or a needle holder for needle handling

commonErrors.error: Passing a sharp directly from hand to hand.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the sharps dish, one sharp at a time.
Never recap or resheath; place the needle in the container.

commonErrors.error: Filling a sharps container past the facility fill line.
commonErrors.prevention: Close and replace the container at the fill line, and never reopen it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Sharps waste leaves the site with a licensed operator, who destroys it by incineration. This lesson does not authorise anyone to transport, treat or dispose of sharps waste.
Check the applicable standard for sharps containers and any fill limit before use. Neither has been checked against an Australian source, and the fill figure is not adopted.
Stop work if a sharp is loose in the field, or if a glove tears during a case. Replace the glove and remove the instrument before continuing.
Completing this lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Learner describes the dish transfer rule and the one-sharp-at-a-time rule.
Learner states the rule for used needles and gives the reason they are not recapped.
Learner states the cleaner steps when a sharp is found.
documentationEvidence: Hazard record for any sharp found outside a container, with location, time and the person alerted.
Record of a glove change or instrument removal during a case, where the theatre keeps one.
summary: Sharps move in a dish, one at a time, and are never handed directly.
Used needles are not recapped, and sharps go into an approved container at the fill line.
A cleaner who finds a sharp stops, keeps others clear, and alerts the theatre team.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should sharp instruments move between a surgeon and an assistant in the theatre?
options: Handed directly from hand to hand across the table
Transferred in a sharps dish, one sharp at a time
Left on the drape until the case ends and passed later
Passed loose in the gown pocket for speed

knowledgeChecks.question: A cleaner finds a used needle on the floor. What is the correct first step?
options: Pick it up with a gloved hand and place it in the bin
Recap it so it cannot cause injury and then bin it with the rest
Stop, keep others clear, and alert the nearest theatre team member
Leave it and clean around it and carry on with the rest of the room

knowledgeChecks.question: Which rule applies to used needles?
options: Recap them before disposal and then bin them with the rest
Do not resheath them; place them in a facility-approved bin
Bend them so they fit the bin and then press them down by hand
Store them on the trolley through the rest of the list

Conflict and resolution: the theatre document asks for a closure point of three-quarters full; the learner guide says not to overfill and gives no fraction. The learner guide governs and the fraction is not adopted (UNCONFIRMED). For a glove tear the theatre document asks for scrub solution on the hands; for a wound the learner guide asks for soap and water. Each applies to its own body part.
Conflict and resolution: the theatre document asks for a sharps dish; the learner guide asks for a puncture-resistant tray. The learner guide governs the equipment standard, so any dish must meet it.
UNCONFIRMED: AS 4031 (sharps container standard) named in the learner guide, not checked.

officialReferences.title: AS 4031 (sharps containers)
officialReferences.covers: UNCONFIRMED: standard named in the learner guide, not checked against the standard text or an official page in this pass. The fill-line and closure rules are also UNCONFIRMED.

officialReferences.title: Sharps waste transport and treatment (state or territory)
officialReferences.covers: Victoria only: clinical waste must be treated before final disposal, with incineration and autoclaving given as examples, and the generator must send waste only to permitted treatment facilities. The page refers to permissions for transport and does not state a licensed-transporter rule, so other states and the licensed-operator point remain unconfirmed. Publisher: EPA Victoria.
